per_window.ps-ns: Unresolved for the native domain: the 2001 relaxation paper that would hold R1/R2/NOE data was read as an abstract only, so no order parameters are available (NTRC-J5, r4, search_insufficient). Spin-label EPR on engineered cysteines reports label mobility, not backbone S2: in full-length MBP-NtrC the position-86 label moves with τR 2.5–3 ns unphosphorylated and slows to near 10 ns on phosphorylation (J41, J42; r45, r46), helix-4 position 89 slows less (J43, r47), the isolated receiver fusion stays at τR ≈ 1.5 ns in both states (J46, r51), and the S160F and Δ444–469 controls tie the restriction to phosphorylation and probably to intermolecular contacts (J47–J51; r52–r56). Labels at V115 and C30 impair function and are flagged as perturbed (J44, J45; r48, r50). All EPR judgments are unresolved for the window: the authors trace the spectral change to interdomain contacts, and the isolated-fusion τR shifts with fragment size, so label τR is not a backbone order parameter of the receiver domain.
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window. Unphosphorylated WT at 25 °C in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.75 interconverts between inactive and active conformations: 15N CPMG gives kex 13,580 ± 850 s−1 with 14% active from the D88 ruler (J1, r20); methyl 1H CPMG gives kex 15,458 ± 452 s−1 at 18 author-listed residues with the population fixed at 14% (J2, r7, r9); I55 fits poorly (J3, r8); the 2001 abstract agrees qualitatively (J4, r4). Phosphorylation and its mimic shift this equilibrium: BeF3−-bound WT exchanges at about 1,950 s−1 with the active state dominant (J18, r23, r14), and a second faster Y101-linked process appears once activation exchange is slow enough to separate (J19, r14; S85D and Y101F, J32, J33, r12, r13); the authors state it cannot be tested in unphosphorylated WT because its exchange near 14,000 s−1 is too fast for 1000 Hz CPMG. Activating mutants D86N and D86N/A89T exchange faster with 43% and 65% active (J24, J25; r21, r22); hydrogen-bond mutants S85D, S85G, Y101F, Q96N and S85D/Y101F slow exchange to 2,800–3,800 s−1 while S85N restores 16,900 s−1 (J26–J31; r24–r29). Y101L keeps activation exchange (2,200 s−1, J34, r15) but loses the faster process except at S13, where sodium binding is suspected (J35, J36; r16, r17); BeF3−-bound Y101L exchanges at 1,500 ± 600 s−1 (J37, r18) and the unnamed partially active mutant of the 2001 abstract stays unresolved (J38, r6). For truly phosphorylated WT only the 2001 abstract speaks (J14, r5, unresolved).
per_window.slower_than_ms: Only denaturant or folding experiments: at the 2.4 M GdmHCl midpoint the domain unfolds slower than 0.1 s−1 and helix 4 unfolds cooperatively with the rest (J9, r30); folding in urea is limited by K104-P105 prolyl isomerization (J11, r35). BeFx titration shows slow-limit coexistence of free and bound resonances, which is binding kinetics (J20, r41). HDX-MS, FRET, time-resolved and multitemperature structural methods were searched with no hits (J13).
per_window.undetermined: MD of unphosphorylated WT gives a slowest relaxation of about 100 μs between a heterogeneous inactive and a uniform active ensemble (J6, r1, md_only) and Y101 rotamer switching on about 1 μs within an active-like state at 320 K (J7, r19, md_only); a Gō model gives folding order with no physical clock (J12, r36, r37). Structures: apo 2MSL ensemble heterogeneity (J8, r2), BeF3− 2MSK helix α4 rotation (J21, r3), abstract-only BeF3− and phosphorylated structures (J22, r10, r11; J16, r58), iron-chelate proximity changes in full-length fusions (J17, J23; r44, r43) and unfolding-kinetics cross-checks without transcribed rates (J10, J15, J39, J40; r31–r34) are all unresolved for timescale. Not judged: Spo0F folding and Gō simulation (r38, r39, homolog), static NtrC/CheY comparison (r40, abstract only), CheY BeFx titration (r42, homolog binding), S160C label (r49, outside the 124-residue entry) and the C-terminal DNA-binding domain structure (r57, outside the entry).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: at 25 °C in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.75, the unphosphorylated wild-type receiver domain switches between inactive and active conformations with kex 13,580 ± 850 s−1 and 14% active state by 15N backbone dispersion (D88 population ruler); this exchange is too fast to be suppressed by 1000 Hz CPMG (JMB 2014), so the rate rests on dispersion plus independently measured exchange-free R2 (Cell 2009 Methods), and methyl 1H dispersion at 18 switch-interface residues gives a similar 15,458 ± 452 s−1 with that 14% population fixed rather than fitted.
open_conflicts: Same unphosphorylated WT state, two dispersion methods: 15N backbone kex 13,580 ± 850 s−1 (r20) versus methyl 1H kex 15,458 ± 452 s−1 (r7); the authors call them in excellent agreement, but the methyl fit fixed pB at the 15N-derived 14%, so the population is not an independent replicate.

BeF3−-bound WT rate printed three ways: 1,940 ± 290 s−1 (2009 Fig. 2D, r23), 1,950 ± 290 s−1 (2014 main text, r14) and 1,950 ± 200 s−1 (2014 Fig. 1C, r14); S85D (2,900 ± 200) and Y101F (3,300 ± 800) are identical in the 2009 and 2014 papers (r24/r12, r27/r13), so they are probably one data set each and not replicates.
Methyl probe count: the methyl paper's narrative says 21 exchanging probes while Table 1 lists 22 methyl groups including the excluded I55-γ2 (r7, r9).
questions_for_gina: Which sample is the RelaxDB 4762 R1/R2/NOE set: unphosphorylated, phosphorylated or the partially active mutant from the 2001 relaxation study (r4–r6, abstract only), and at what temperature and buffer? Without it the ps-ns window cannot be judged.

All Kern-lab NMR samples used 50 mM sodium phosphate for a phosphorylatable receiver domain with no phosphate-free control, and the 2014 authors suspect sodium binding at S13; should the atlas carry the 14% active population and kex values as the WT apo answer as they stand, or flag them as buffer-dependent until a control exists?
protein_summary.buffer_note: All 15N and methyl dispersion and HSQC unfolding samples (r7–r9, r12–r30) are the isolated receiver domain in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.75 with 10% D2O at 25 °C (0.75 mM, or 0.3 mM for BeF3−-activated and Y101L samples in 2014); Mg2+ is not stated, and no phosphate-free control exists. The methyl sample is deuterated with CHD2 labelling. Folding kinetics (r35) used 10 mM potassium phosphate pH 7.0 with urea. The 2015 structures (r2, r3) are at 35 °C with buffer not restated. EPR samples (r45–r56) are MBP fusions with C30V/C364A and an engineered cysteine, in Tris-acetate pH 7.8 with 0.1 mM EDTA at 22–23 °C; iron-chelate cleavage samples (r43, r44) contain both 8 mM MgCl2 and 1 mM EDTA. BeF3− is a phosphorylation mimic and is kept separate from carbamoyl-phosphate or steady-state phosphorylation. MD runs are at 300 K (r1) and 320 K (r19).
